title: Wind-snapped Scots Pine Log Section (Pinus sylvestris) — Splintered Break, Blow-down
era: natural (Ukrainian/Russian pine bor and forest-steppe landscape, contemporary)

sources.scots_pine_wiki: Pinus sylvestris — Wikipedia: 'mature 25–35 m (exceptionally >45 m), trunk to ~1 m diameter, orange-brown upper bark; foundation species on poor dry sandy sites'
sources.scots_pine_jrc: EU JRC Forest Atlas via research brief: 'trunk diameter range 0.5–1.3 m (exceptionally >1.7 m)'
sources.bark_texture_conifers: conifers.org + Wikipedia — 'Scots pine bark is TWO-TONE: lower trunk thick scaly grey-brown deeply fissured plates up to ~5 cm thick; upper trunk + branches thin flaking orange-red/copper'
sources.bor_ground_layer: EUNIS habitat 1283 — Pleurozium schreberi, Dicranum sp. moss ground/timber layer in bor (зеленомошник type); Kytöviita 2009, Functional Ecology
sources.research_brief: Ecology + visual character of Ukrainian/Russian regional landscape biomes — ENGENDROS PURGE world plan + model dossiers (2026-06-10)

log_trunk.prop_diameter_note: Design value: represents a younger/smaller specimen below the mature DBH range of 500–1300 mm. Chosen for FPS prop scale (smaller windfall, crouchable). Exact sub-adult DBH data not sourced → flagged in needs[].
log_trunk.prop_section_length_note: Design value — no sourced windfall-section statistics for Pinus sylvestris wind-throw. 1.2 m chosen as compact debris prop. Flagged in needs[].
log_trunk.bark_character: Lower: thick grey-brown scaly fissured plates; upper/exposed: thin flaking orange-red/copper

moss_coverage.habitat: Fallen/dead timber in pine bor (зеленомошник biome); moss colonises upper surface of wind-thrown logs
moss_coverage.patch_thickness_note: Design value — specific moss-patch depth on fallen pine bark not quantified in sources. 30 mm (3 cm) is a plausible field estimate. Flagged in needs[].

split_break.desc: Wind-snapped break shows radially-split wood fibres (splinters) projecting up and forward from the break face. The exposed heartwood face is pale/cream, the splinters are darker weathered wood.
split_break.src: research_brief (war-killed forest description: 'field of stumps', 'stripped broken trunks', 'black sticks'); bark_texture_conifers for wood colour
split_break.splinter_note: Splinter dimensions are design values proportional to log radius (200 mm ≈ 1.4× radius). No sourced measurements for snap-fracture splinter geometry.

derivation.derivation: bark_shadow h = 43% of diameter (60/140=43% radius); wood_face wh = diameter - 2×bark_th ≈ 220mm; splinters centred 30 mm forward of break face (z=0.60 + 0.03 offset); moss patch ≈ 57% trunk diameter wide × 2.1× radius long; bark_knot proportional scar ~50% radius wide

main_body.desc: Full-length cylinder, lying horizontal along Z axis, orange-brown pine bark

bark_shadow.desc: Dark lower-bark band at ground contact — old grey-brown fissured plates + shadow

wood_face.desc: Pale exposed heartwood cross-section at the break (snap) end

splinters.desc: Three upright wood-fibre splinters at the break end: one central (taller), two flanking (shorter/darker)

moss_patch.desc: Pleurozium moss strip on the upper log surface, mid-section

bark_knot.desc: Dark branch-knot scar embedded in the upper bark surface near the clean end

game_model_purpose: World prop — wind-snapped broken log for bor, forest-steppe, and war-damaged forest biomes; debris/obstacle scenery distinct from log_fallen (larger, unbroken) and stump_cut (vertical)
needs: Sub-adult Pinus sylvestris DBH data — prop diameter 280 mm is below published mature range (500–1300 mm); no forestry source cited for younger-stand diameter
Wind-throw log section length — 1200 mm is a design value; no sourced windfall-section statistics for pine wind-throw
Snap-fracture splinter geometry — splinter dimensions (height 200 mm, count 3) are design estimates; no sourced measurements for conifer wind-snap fracture morphology
Moss-on-bark thickness — 30 mm patch thickness is a design estimate; EUNIS 1283 gives species presence but no geometric measurement for this application
